desc:
Given an integer array nums (values may be negative or zero) and an integer target, choose as many non-overlapping non-empty contiguous subarrays as possible such that each chosen subarray has a sum equal to target. Return the maximum number of subarrays you can choose.

nums = [-1, 3, 5, 1, 4, 2, -9], target = 6
disjoint blocks with sum 6: [5, 1] and [4, 2]
result = 2
hints: Finding every subarray with sum target is the easy part (prefix sums + hash set). The question is which of them to keep.
This is like interval scheduling: among blocks that end earliest, taking the one that finishes first never hurts the future.
Scan left to right with a set of prefix sums since the last chosen block (starting with {0}). When running - target is in the set, count a block and reset the set and the running sum.
editorial: Each subarray with sum target is an interval. Choosing the maximum number of pairwise disjoint intervals is solved greedily by always taking the interval with the earliest right end: it leaves the most room for the rest.

While scanning, keep the prefix sums observed since the end of the last chosen block (plus 0 for the empty start). At each position, if running - target is in that set then some block ending here has sum target and lies entirely after the last chosen block; it is the earliest-ending one available, so take it, increment the answer, and restart with an empty history. Otherwise record the running sum. The scan is O(n) time and O(n) space.
